Tottenham Hotspur have reportedly sent scouts to keep a close eye on Benfica striker Vangelis Pavlidis.

Spurs made a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign under Roberto De Zerbi, failing to win any of their opening six league games.

However, the club kept faith with their manager, and results have since started to improve, with Tottenham winning four of their last five league matches to climb to 10th in the Premier League table.

Despite spending heavily during the summer transfer window, De Zerbi feels his squad still needs strengthening, with bolstering the forward line becoming a priority.

Spurs have recently been linked with a move for Freiburg forward Igor Matanovic, but it appears they are also exploring alternative options.

According to a report from Record, Tottenham are showing interest in the 28-year-old Benfica forward, who has been in outstanding form for the Portuguese giants.

After scoring 80 goals in 137 appearances for AZ Alkmaar, Pavlidis moved to Benfica in the summer of 2024 and has continued his prolific goalscoring form.

The Greece international scored 30 goals in each of his previous two seasons and has already registered 19 goals and four assists this term.

The report claims that Tottenham have sent scouts on several occasions this season to assess the striker, with the club continuing to monitor his situation closely.

Dominic Solanke has struggled with fitness complications but offered signs of a return to form after scoring in last Saturday's 2-0 win over Ipswich Town.

However, Richarlison is almost certain to leave the club after his relationship with De Zerbi reportedly broke down completely following his failed move to Everton in the summer.

The Brazilian has been linked with moves to clubs in Turkey and the Saudi Pro League, while Vasco da Gama are also keen to bring him back to his homeland.

By Saikat Mandal | 26 Nov 2026 07:41.

Tottenham Hotspur may have suffered a setback in their pursuit of Inter Milan central midfielder Hakan Calhanoglu ahead of the January transfer window or next summer.

After enduring the worst possible start to the 2026-27 campaign, during which Spurs failed to win any of their opening seven games, they have bounced back strongly in the league.

The north London club have picked up four wins in their last five matches, climbing to 10th in the Premier League table with 15 points, six adrift of fourth-placed Liverpool.

Spurs spent heavily to strengthen their midfield during the summer, bringing in Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, but the club are still looking to add further quality in that department.

Recent reports have suggested that Tottenham have earmarked Calhanoglu as a target for next summer, although Galatasaray, Juventus and Como are also interested in the midfielder.

According to a report from Football Insider, Spurs may have suffered a blow in the race, with Calhanoglu preferring to remain at Inter Milan.

The 32-year-old midfielder is out of contract with the Italian giants at the end of the season, but preliminary talks have begun over an extension as he is keen to continue his career at San Siro.

Since joining from AC Milan in the summer of 2021, Calhanoglu has scored 53 goals in 226 appearances for the Nerazzurri.

The central midfielder registered 19 goal contributions in 30 games last term and has already scored three goals in his opening 10 league appearances this season.

While Spurs can match Calhanoglu's wage demands, they are not prepared to pay a transfer fee at this stage, instead hoping to sign him on a free transfer.

This leaves Tottenham anxiously waiting to see whether the Turkish midfielder can reach an agreement with Inter over a newly introduced deal.

Calhanoglu can operate as a defensive midfielder and is renowned for his excellent long-range shooting, making him an exciting potential addition to De Zerbi's squad, even at this stage of his career.

Liverpool have been dealt a fresh injury concern in the first half of their Champions League fixture against Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds got off to a strong start at the Jan Breydel Stadium as they pounced on a loose pass by Yann Sommer to take the lead through a close-range finish from Alexander Isak.

However, Andoni Iraola was left wincing in the technical area when, shortly before half-time, Victor Munoz went to ground and stayed there after a surging run into the hosts’ penalty area was abruptly halted.

It quickly became clear that the Liverpool winger was in pain, and a stretcher was readied before the Spaniard got to his feet and was able to limp off, with Rio Ngumoha coming on in his place (Sky Sports).

(Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images).

Sources indicate that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The sight of Munoz standing up and walking (gingerly) off the pitch came as a relief, but to lose the 23-year-old in such innocuous circumstances represents a major body blow to Liverpool.

The summer signing from Osasuna has had to rely mostly on substitute appearances so far in his Reds career, but he was handed a start by Iraola tonight off the back of his fine showing off the bench against Manchester United on Sunday.

The Spanish winger rounded off the scoring in that match and had Club Brugge terrified with some mazy, proactive dribbling before that unfortunate injury setback when he overstretched to try and get to the ball.

It remains to be seen just how seriously Munoz has been hurt and whether he’ll face a lengthy spell on the sidelines, but we can only keep our fingers crossed that it isn’t as bad as what it initially seemed.

Iraola might be able to provide us with an upgrade after full-time, even if it’d only be a preliminary indication.

Manchester United reportedly remain open to selling Marcus Rashford in January if they receive a suitable offer for the forward.

Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona, and it appeared that his future lay away from Old Trafford after he fell out with former manager Ruben Amorim.

Man Utd publicly backed his reintegration into the squad after Barcelona opted against signing him permanently, but the England international has so far cut a disappointing figure.

Rashford has made six Premier League appearances this season, starting four of them, but is yet to register a goal or assist.

With Mauricio Pochettino looking to reshape the attacking line-up in his own image, Rashford could once again find himself facing an uncertain future.

Speaking on the Market Madness podcast, transfer expert Ben Jacobs has suggested that the Red Devils would still consider suitable offers for Rashford.

The forward remains under contract at United until 2028, meaning the club are under no immediate pressure to sell him.

At the same time, the Red Devils could consider letting him leave as they look to add depth and quality to their forward department in January or potentially next summer.

It has been revealed that rashford is right now sidelined with a hip injury and missed both of Pochettino's first two games in charge. However, the club expect him to return before the end of the month, potentially in time for the clash against Brentford.

Joshua Zirkzee came on at half-time against Liverpool, but there is a strong possibility that the Dutch striker could be offloaded, with several Serie A clubs reportedly keen on his signature.

Pochettino also needs to reshape his defence, with signing a latest centre-back a priority, potentially putting Lisandro Martinez's future at the club in doubt.

There are also doubts over the long-term future of captain Bruno Fernandes, who has already rejected two contract offers from the club.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 17:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:02 EST, 25 November 2026.

The message from Enzo Maresca ought to be clear when Manchester City convene for their meeting at the training ground this weekend before heading down to London. Clear because there is no other appropriate message to impart, really.

Sources indicate that he has to say that Arsenal away must be considered the perfect game for his players at this point. The opportunity to reignite their season, to stand up, to show the Premier League they are not going anywhere just quite yet. Squads who went before them would certainly approach a fixture of this magnitude with that attitude. A squad with Kevin De Bruyne as its linchpin would.

City were still searching for answers against Napoli, a point rescued late on by Rayan Cherki. But despite the growing frustration in the stands, that unmistakable guttural desperation for just a bit more of something, it was better. More joined up thinking, at least.

An inverted full back did that for them and it perhaps should be the blueprint for the manager when they arrive at the Emirates on Sunday. City were eminently more comfortable with that; knew where they stood. Nico O'Reilly was not particularly brilliant in that position yet his presence, the safety net of somebody alongside Ayyoub Bouaddi in possession and in turn freeing up Elliot Anderson will surely make City more formidable as the weeks go by.

The set-up presented another tactical tweak for Maresca as he searches for answers and consistency. Defensively, City were twice undone by individual mistakes rather than the overarching blueprint, one that stifled the enduring class of De Bruyne.

A gentle hum, the half-hearted chants for a returning king, resembled an afternoon session in front of a crowd drowsy from their liquid lunches before a seesawing four-goal second half felt more befitting of City's guest for the evening, UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin – intriguingly entertained by chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak in the directors' box.

Rayan Cherki rescued a point late on but this was another difficult night for Man City.

Former Man United striker Rasmus Hojlund celebrates his goal against his old rivals.

Ayyoub Bouaddi scored his first goal for Manchester City since joining from Lille.

City, sporting a fourth kit that had an unfortunate Guantanamo quality to it, certainly had more of a clue than they did here on Saturday. There were clearer patterns – noticeably Marc Guehi piercing midfield lines with one incisive pass for O'Reilly – but this is a team whose confidence has been shaken in recent weeks and that will not return overnight. 'We were aggressive off the ball,' noted Maresca, while bemoaning conceding for a tenth consecutive match. 'Defensively we were good, pressing good.'.

Regardless, City's supporters definitely demanded more caution thrown to the wind and some of their players wore those looks too. Anderson's dangerous crosses from that right-hand channel – the area presided over by De Bruyne for a decade – occasionally proved unsettling for Napoli, while Allan should have scored from a ricocheting corner as captain Erling Haaland claimed a penalty for being dragged down.

Man City (4-2-3-1): Donnarumma 6; Nunes 5, Guehi 5, Gvardiol 6, O'Reilly 5; Bouaddi 7, Anderson 6; Cherki 7, Fernandez 6 (Ndiaye 63, 6), Allan 5 (Doku 54, 7); Haaland 5.

Napoli (4-1-4-1): Milinkovic-Savic 6; Spinazzola 7, Beukema 6, Rrahmani 7, Olivera 6; Gilmour 8; Politano 6, McTominay 6, De Bruyne 6, Lang 7; Hojlund 7.

Manager: Massimiliano Allegri 7.

In a sign that Maresca was placing more players in threatening areas, O'Reilly had headed over a Matheus Nunes cross – yet chances had been at a premium, those who should be protagonists taking too many safe options rather than pushing chests out and relishing responsibility.

Industry observers note that and when there was risk, Napoli pounced. Cherki the culprit, flicking a ball around the corner aimlessly into the middle of his own half. Billy Gilmour gave thanks, punched towards Rasmus Hojlund and he spun Guehi to flash under Donnarumma ten minutes into the second half. Hojlund celebrated by shouting 'one club in Manchester' while holding a single finger aloft. 'It's good banter,' he said and we'll take his word for that.

City had been warned of the danger, when Noa Lang went clean through before checking back upon realising he didn't possess the acceleration to complete the job.

Sources indicate that maresca's assistant, Danny Walker, shook his head on the bench as they pored over the goal's replay. Enzo Fernandez was planting his boot into one of Vanja Milinkovic-Savic's posts when the goalkeeper nonchalantly plucked a floated cross from the night sky.

Sources indicate that city had stirred somewhat though, helped by the inclusion of Jeremy Doku – ironically introduced seconds before Hojlund's opener – and it was the Belgian who made their equaliser seven minutes after the hour. He waited and waited inside Napoli's box for defenders to commit, finding Bouaddi alone and the teenager wrapped his left foot around the pass and was quickly racing back to halfway.

There had appeared a head of steam, only for O'Reilly to be caught well out of position as Napoli countered – City carved open – and Lang thundered a volley past Donnarumma with 14 minutes left. Cherki made amends for his earlier error by hammering into the far corner but was less than pleased.

Recent findings suggest that 'We played good but we don't give a lot of energy,' Cherki said. 'We need to do more, we need to win these games, and today I don't care (about) scoring my goal. I want to win this game. We're going to London to win.'.

In fact, maybe that is the team talk.

Liverpool midfielder Trey Nyoni was praised for a ‘superb’ performance against Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The 19-year-old was restored to the Reds’ starting XI for the match at the Jan Breydel Stadium, with Alexis Mac Allister dropping to the bench as Andoni Iraola rewarded the youngster for his fine form of late.

The teenager played for 73 minutes in Belgium before he was replaced by the Argentine as the visitors sought to regain control amid a concerted spell of pressure from the home side.

Football writer Sam McGuire took to X at half-time to praise the Liverpool midfielder’s showing as he posted: ‘Trey Nyoni bossing it again. Joint most touches and he’s completed 93% of his passes.’.

Elsewhere, Ian Doyle handed the youngster 8/10 in his half-time player rating for the Liverpool Echo, writing that the Reds’ number 42 ‘demonstrated superb composure in possession, especially when dealing with an increasing number of defensive situations ahead of half-time.’.

In a recent development, want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

Handed a fourth Champions League start of the season, Nyoni repaid Iraola’s faith with a fine performance against Club Brugge tonight.

As Doyle referenced, the 19-year-old made some vital defensive contributions in Belgium, dispossessing Carlos Forbs just before half-time and stopping the winger in his tracks in a dangerous position once again just after the hour mark.

Steven Gerrard proclaimed before kick-off that the teenager is ‘like a Rolls Royce’ and ‘never lets the team down’ (TNT Sports, via Sky Sports), and our number 42 underlined that reputation with an excellent showing on Wednesday, as reflected in his underlying figures from Sofascore.

It seemed harsh on Nyoni to be substituted when he was, but Iraola clearly felt that he needed more experience on the pitch with the simultaneous introduction of Mac Allister and Virgil van Dijk.

The double change was vindicated by Liverpool extending their tenuous 1-0 lead to a comfortable 3-0 margin in the final 20 minutes, but the teenage midfielder can still feel rightly proud of his performance tonight.

AC Milan are five points behind the somewhat surprise league-leaders Lazio, but belief is growing regarding a Scudetto push.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, Milan re-emerged from the two-week international break and put in arguably their best performance of the season against Frosinone. They scored five goals and it could have been more, racking up a third league win in a row to move back into the top four.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In a recent development, the table remains quite tight at the top, with Inter the only team to slip up over the weekend, and the Rossoneri are firmly in the running. The paper highlights give reasons that a title fight is very possible.

Gerry Cardinale and Ruben Amorim are inextricably linked, and that might seem obvious, given that one is the owner and the other the coach. In reality, the bond is deeper than usual, for one simple reason.

Sources indicate that amorim has been handed the keys to create the ‘new Milan’, one that Cardinale has decided to manage completely differently since the end of May. The Portuguese is the coach to whom RedBird have given the longest contract so far, and Cardinale believes he’s the right man at the right time.

In a recent development, he’s demonstrating this concretely not only with his constant presence and his reassuring words, but also with his intention to improve the squad swiftly and with the arrival of a key management figure like Markus Krösche. Now, Amorim will receive even greater support.

Gonçalo Inacio, Nicolo Tresoldi, Endrick. These are just some of the names circulating – and these aren’t rumours, but actual targets – ahead of a potentially crucial January transfer window.

In a recent development, the question is obvious: with a couple of top-notch signings for the second half of the season, how far could this team go? Staying up there for starters remains the minimum objective, with Champions League football a must.

Then, Amorim and co. hope that the rest will follow, if their rivals begin to lose pace. The coach is starting to make his team look like they are clicking, but Cardinale has realised the need to accelerate to fill the remaining gaps in the squad.

Amorim (fortunately) quickly realised that the average tactical level of his colleagues in Italy is too high to allow himself to present his Milan team in the same way every single way. So, the 3-4-2-1 that was previously seemingly set in stone has become plasticine in his hands.

Industry observers note that the manager moulds and shapes the playing system based on the opponents, rather than his own needs. Since Ruben the fundamentalist became Ruben the quick-change artist, we’ve seen a bit of everything: 4-2-3-1, 4-3-3, 4-4-1-1, 3-5-2.

The former Sporting CP coach coach locks himself in the lab throughout the week and tailors the formation he deems best. Sometimes he gets it wrong, but most of the time he gets it right.

Milan have won five of their last six league games and, game by game, they are increasingly able to camouflage themselves effectively tactically. Opponents never know what formation they will face, while Amorim has several players capable of playing well in multiple roles, which helps.

The data is remarkable and reads as follows: only Rocco (29) and Czeizler (31) coached Milan sides that have scored more goals than Amorim’s (28) in their first 12 Serie A games in charge.

In short, despite all the problems involved (Goncalo Ramos in particular, more on him to come) the coach’s attacking vocation is clearly visible. Furthermore, it is a Milan with a high conversion rate in proportion to the shots on target.

According to recent reports, it is also a Diavolo side that have somehow found a way to make up for Ramos’ poor contribution in terms of goals. Alphadjo Cisse, Diego Moreira, Christian Pulisic and Adrien Rabiot take turns to set each other up and score, a sign of a growing offensive physiognomy.

Industry observers note that more often than not, a striker simply needs to get a goal in order to build confidence and then begin a virtuous cycle. Milan hope that this is the case for Ramos, who ended his month-long goal drought on Sunday.

However, the reflection goes further: while the Rossoneri having the luxury of being able to score without goals from their No.9 (who is currently on three in the league), surely things can only get better from here?

In short, if the Portuguese international actually does start firing more regularly, then Milan might unlock another dimension to their attack that could really see them surge towards that elusive Scudetto.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pierre Sage felt Crystal Palace were “really far off” his expectations after suffering a 3-2 away Europa League defeat by his former side Lyon.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half devoid of any shots on target for the visitors.

Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break, before Pavel Sulc restored the two-goal lead, and substitute Daichi Kamada’s late goal proved a mere consolation.

“At the end, we were frustrated by the result, but in the first half we have to be frustrated in the way we play,” noted Sage, speaking to PalaceTV.

In a recent development, “I think we didn’t play this first half. We are really far off our standards in the mental side of the play, in the tactical side of the play, because the players are too high between our lines and we really struggled a lot with that.

It has been revealed that “When you give back the ball to your opponent, you suffer a lot and we were better in the second half. You cannot win this kind of game by playing only one half.”.

Sage’s side got the better of his predecessor, Oliver Glasner, after they bounced back to beat Nottingham Forest 3-1 at Selhurst Park on Sunday.

After that victory, the Frenchman called for more consistency from his team, but on Thursday night was left ruing missed opportunities and goals conceded too easily by last season’s Conference League winners.

Sources indicate that sage was sacked by Lyon in January 2025 after a 14-month spell with the Ligue 1 outfit. Like Glasner’s, his own reunion ended in disappointment.

He told Uefa: “It’s a very disappointing return because we lost. I can’t take satisfaction from coming back home or seeing familiar faces when the result isn’t there.

“The scoreline may have been close, but there was a big difference in the way the two teams played.

“We improved considerably after the break and gave ourselves a chance, but conceding that third goal made things difficult.

“I think our second-half efforts deserved an equaliser, although winning would have been a generous reward given that we only really played [to our level] for one half.”.

The veteran captain said: “It has been a long time coming. The fans were up for it, the players were up for it so we’re very happy with the performance.”.

When asked about Evanilson’s header, which Smith supplied the assist for, he replied: “It wasn’t my best cross but I put it in an area, what a finish from him and I think we deserved that little bit of luck.

“From there on we went on to win the game but in the second half we got a little bit tired but the quality that came off the bench is great and we look forward to Sunday now.

“It’s a great header, he deserved it because he has worked very hard this season and many more to come from him.”.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of Thursday night’s European football with Crystal Palace, Sunderland and Bournemouth in Europa League action, and Brighton hosting Kauno Zalgiris in the Uefa Conference League.

Palace manager Pierre Sage managed Lyon between November 2023 and January 2025, and another sub-plot is American businessman John Textor’s involvement with the French club. The former Palace shareholder was the reason the club missed out on Europa League participation last season because Lyon were in the same competition and thus Palace were considered in breach of multi-club ownership rules. Textor sold his stake in Palace, but despite the club’s best efforts they had to settle for the Conference League, a competition they subsequently won.

In a recent development, palace could have been three or four down against Nottingham Forest at the weekend but fought back for a much-needed Premier League victory. They made a winning start in Europe, beating Lech Poznan 4-0 at Selhurst Park in their opening Europa League game.

Bournemouth and Sunderland also made winning starts, despite both teams’ poor form domestically. Sunderland travel to Portuguese side Torreense, while Sturm Graz are the opposition for Bournemouth’s first ever European game at the Vitality Stadium (or Dean Court if you prefer). Bournemouth continue to be without Justin Kluivert, Eli Junior Kroupi and Alex Scott because of injury.

It has been revealed that brighton are favourites to win the Conference League and play their first game in the competition against Lithuanian club Kauno Zalgiris. Lifting the trophy in Istanbul at the end of the season would assure Brighton of a place in next season’s Europa League, though given their Premier League form and Manchester City’s predicament, Champions League qualification could be a realistic aspiration. Brighton won with 10 men at Sunderland on Saturday, and were successful in their appeal against Pascal Struijk’s red card.

Chris Sutton has said that Florian Wirtz looks like a ‘different’ player for Liverpool this season compared to last.

The Germany playmaker endured plenty of criticism during his first year in English football following his £100m+ move from Bayer Leverkusen, and that continued into the early weeks of this campaign.

However, the 23-year-old has been excellent since the extended international window earlier in the autumn, and he netted the Reds’ second goal in their 3-0 victory away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

It’s the third consecutive game in which Liverpool’s number 7 has scored, and he now has four goals and five assists across his last 10 matches in all competitions for the Reds (Transfermarkt).

Speaking on BBC Radio 5 Live towards the end of the win in Belgium, Sutton was keen to praise Wirtz for his performance against Ivan Leko’s side.

The former Blackburn and Chelsea striker remarked: “It’s a different Florian Wirtz this season. He’s just oozing with confidence.”.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The German’s prolific form of late is reminiscent of the purple patch that he enjoyed over the festive period last year and into January, when he scored six times in 10 matches.

It isn’t just his improvement in terms of goal contributions which has stood out, though. As Cody Gakpo rightly highlighted in recent weeks, the 23-year-old boasts ‘incredible football intelligence‘ and is now linking up brilliantly with his attacking teammates.

Liverpool Echo reporter Ian Doyle awarded Wirtz 8/10 in his post-match player ratings, writing that our number 7 ‘buzzed with real intent behind [Alexander] Isak’ and was ‘constantly first on to second balls, which he used well, whilst also netting ‘with aplomb’ for his goal.

The German completed two dribbles and won six duels against Club Brugge (Sofascore), and having found the confidence to match his ability of late, he’s now grown into one of the Reds’ best performers.

In a recent development, those critics who were tripping over themselves to lay into the 23-year-old must now be feeling rather foolish as they watch him exert an ever-greater influence for Andoni Iraola’s side. Long may it continue!

Christos Tzolis has not improved Arsenal's left-hand side of attack since arriving.

The Gunners needed to add another name to the wide forward areas, as that was a clear weakness in their squad.

Greek international Tzolis was deemed to be that player, with Arsenal forking out £34million to bring him to the Emirates from Club Brugge.

His arrival then allowed Arsenal to sell Gabriel Martinelli for a club-record £60m fee, but in many ways, the Gunners may be weaker for that fact.

Tzolis, 24, has been a regular when fit, starting seven of his eight Premier League appearances so far.

But he may already be a player that Mikel Arteta is looking to upgrade on in the coming transfer windows.

Tzolis has struggled to make the adaptation from the Belgian Pro League to the Premier League.

While he produced 40 goal contributions (17 goals and 23 assists) in 2025-26, he has been far off the pace for Arsenal.

Tzolis has only managed to obtain one league assist and has yet to score in any competition for Arteta's side.

Additionally, as per FotMob, his underlying numbers do not make for a positive reading either.

This season, Tzolis has produced just 0.45 xG across his 538 Premier League minutes, which equates to just 0.08 per 90.

Hardly a threat for his opposition to look out for when facing up against the winger.

Furthermore, his creative numbers are not great either, with just 0.91 expected assists in total.

He sits in the 27th percentile for significant chances created with just one this campaign.

Overall, Arsenal need a lot more from Tzolis, as across the 11 games this season, it is evident he is the weakest link in Arsenal's common starting forward line.

Arsenal will undoubtedly be keeping tabs on the market for possible forward signings, and it appears they are once again looking in Club Brugge's direction.

At Football Insider, we have shared that Arsenal are well-placed to swoop for Carlos Forbs.

The Portuguese winger, like Tzolis, is impressing in the Belgian top flight; the Gunners must be tentative not to follow down the same path.

Tzolis is evidently not equipped for the Premier League, and the same issues could arise with Forbs.

Arsenal should spend more than £80m on a genuinely elite left-sided flyer like Antonia Nusa, who is headed for the very top.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alexander Isak is now into double digits for goals for Liverpool this season, having netted twice in the 3-0 victory away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ record signing endured a tough first campaign at Anfield after his £125m move from Newcastle, scoring just four times and being sidelined for four months due to a broken leg.

Those initial struggles now seem like a distant memory after his brace in Belgium tonight took him onto 10 goals in 16 matches for his club in 2026/27, already more than doubling his tally from the whole of last term.

Isak opened the scoring for Liverpool in the first half at the Jan Breydel Stadium and wrapped up the victory in the 83rd minute by outmuscling Brandon Mechele, advancing into the penalty area and coolly lofting the ball over Yann Sommer in the Club Brugge net.

In a recent development, calling that goal for TNT Sports, Sam Matterface gushed: “That’s brilliant from Isak. He’s got away from Mechele and he’s bursting into the box, and this will seal it…oh, it’s beautiful, delicious! Such a brilliant finish.”.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The manner in which Isak took that clinching goal shows just how much confidence is flowing through his veins right now. Every time he gets the ball in that area of the pitch, he looks like finishing off the chance (aside from an uncharacteric miss against Manchester United on Sunday).

It isn’t just the quality of his finishing which is standing out, either – as Ian Doyle noted for the Liverpool Echo, the 27-year-old helped to create his first goal by pressing the Club Brugge defence and forcing the error from Sommer.

He also looks increasingly at ease with his fellow attackers, with a neat chemistry now forming on the pitch, and his confidence is evident in how he runs at opposition defences with an attitude of “I’ve got you!”.

John Aldridge recently claimed that Isak may well be targeting somewhere in the region of 20 to 25 goals for the season, and the Swede is already halfway to the lower end of that bracket with one more match still to play in November.

Along with fellow 2025 arrival Florian Wirtz, Liverpool’s number 9 is showing everyone why his current club spent such a vast money on him.

If he doesn’t suffer a recurrence of the injury problems which ruined his first campaign with the Reds, he could easily end up hitting or even surpassing the target that Aldridge has set.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

PIF could be looking to exit Newcastle United after seeking new investment at St James' Park this season.

That is according to former Manchester City financial adviser Stefan Borson, who exclusively told Football Insider that the war in the Middle East has changed PIF's stance.

Amidst a "liquidity concern" for the owners on Tyneside, PIF are looking to sell up to 25 per cent of the club by issuing upcoming shares.

This has instantly sparked concerns amongst the fanbase that Newcastle's Saudi owners could be trying to slowly edge out of St James' Park.

It is understood that the upcoming investment would help fund major infrastructure projects, such as building a new stadium or redeveloping the current one.

Sources have told The Guardian that PIF retain a long-term commitment to the club. Yet, concerns are still there over a change of ownership.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Borson explained that the Saudi's "astonishing" financial issues right now could impact the Magpies in the long-term.

"In the financial markets, there's a feeling that the Saudis, at the moment, have a bit of a liquidity issue, which is obviously astonishing," he said.

"Over the last 50 years, the one thing that we've always seen is that the Saudis have been very cash rich and clearly, with the oil situation, have been well placed.

"Now, the war in the Middle East has changed that a little bit right now without great visibility as to how.

"But the noises are that PIF and the Saudis are generally looking to exit or not carry out follow-on fundraising.".

The state-owned fund owns 84 per cent of the Magpies, with the remaining 16 per cent owned by the London-based Reuben brothers.

"At the moment, it's for a 25 per cent problem of new shares. That's dilutive to the existing holders," Borson said to Football Insider.

"What you've got is effectively a fundraiser by the company which will dilute the existing shareholders.".

There have been whispers that Amanda Staveley could return, but any deal would be extremely expensive, and maybe too much for the 53-year-old.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Friedkin Group (TFG) should not be concerned about their sale of Everton after the latest news emerging from Newcastle United.

That is according to former Manchester City financial adviser Stefan Borson, who exclusively told Football Insider that the Toffees could easily been seen as the "more attractive" proposition.

TFG officially announced their decision to explore a sale in October, very soon after a very frustrating summer window at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Newcastle's owners, PIF, are now the latest to seek new investment, and are open to selling 25 per cent of their stake to aid stadium redevelopment.

The Magpies have already been in talks with potential US investors, and understandably, this has raised concerns over a potential sale on Merseyside.

TFG are still yet to find a solution to their desire to leave Everton already, and now there appears to be more competition in the market.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Borson believes that the Toffees' stadium is a significant enough selling point to avoid any concerns about TFG getting stuck.

"Now, the price level is totally different, but they're still selling a story around a football club development, a good stadium and a good training ground possibility," he said.

"And then you've got Everton looking to sell completely. You've got all of the stuff I've just mentioned about: interest rates, inflation, everything else.

It has been revealed that "They're all drivers that are negative to football clubs. Somebody might take it the other way. To take it the other way, is the Everton opportunity now more attractive because they built the stadium?

"That was always a significant selling point, but actually, in an environment where it would cost even more to build that stadium today...

"...Does that make the club much more attractive to be purchased today. Looking to go forward, yes, I can see that.".

Investors choosing Newcastle shouldn't be totally ruled out, though, as PIF have built an incredible club at St James' Park as well.

"Newcastle have a lot of features that are going to be attractive, of course. As do Everton. They're actually in a similar kind of position for the next phase," Borson said.

"Everton have lower revenues, but haven't invested anywhere near what Newcastle have over the last few years on the playing side.

"So there is that blank piece of paper opportunity there for them, especially given that they don't look like they've got the relegation risk.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Alphadjo Cisse is one goal away from double figures for the season, and we have not even reached the end of November yet.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, the numbers that Cisse is putting up are those of a centre-forward. He has six goals in 10 Serie A appearances, at an average of one every 74 minutes. In the Europa League he has three (a hat-trick against RB Salzburg), at one every 84 minutes.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Yet, his role remains a bit of a mystery. Cisse has his own idea of ​​his preferred position on the pitch, even if he’s a bit vague. Speaking after the match against Frosinone, he hinted that he’d like to move into the attacking midfielder position behind the striker.

“I’d have more fun and entertain the fans. It would also be easier to provide assists for my team-mates, something I enjoy and haven’t yet managed to do at AC Milan,” he confessed to Sky.

In a recent development, in Verona’s youth team, where Cisse first emerged, head coach Paolo Sammarco deployed him as a left-sided attacking midfielder. It was a position in which the then 17-year-old then went on to score 16 league goals in a breakout season.

Sources indicate that at Catanzaro, in his first professional stint in Serie B under Alberto Aquilani, the Italian played more or less the same role in a 3-4-2-1 system, sometimes a bit wider. Before the serious injury that caused him to miss the final six months of last season, he has scored six goals in 22 games.

Sources indicate that ruben Amorim initially deployed him as a left-sided winger, also due to Christian Pulisic’s temporary unavailability. He would later move him further forward and more centrally, to take up the spaces a striker would, a position he has played for Italy U21s under Silvio Baldini.

In this position, Cisse can utilise his extraordinary ability to position himself between the ball and the defender, before turning, aiming and often finishing first time. Despite not being physically big (at 180cm tall), he is strong and has a low centre of gravity that makes him tough to bump off the ball.

Sources indicate that ⚽️ GOAL ALPHADJO CISSE! 🔥 https://t.co/aMIgE9PXHc.

— SempreMilan (@SempreMilanCom) November 22, 2026.

According to recent reports, this is where the dilemma arises. At Verona and Catanzaro, Alphadjo Cisse impressed because of his speed and agility. After the injury and under the watch of Amorim, he has become more of a positioning-based player, barely ever tearing down the flank.

So far this season, he’s attempted only 16 dribbles at just over three per game, and has only succeeded on five. With one successful dribble per game on average, his success rate is just over 31% (FotMob data).

It has been revealed that these numbers perhaps help explain Cisse’s progression close to the penalty area, and also a concept that the player himself has repeated in recent months regarding where he is at in his personal development. On Sunday, he declared: “I’m not even halfway to my potential.”.

It has been revealed that who knows if Alpha is referring to his overall growth, with horizons still unexplored, or perhaps his post-injury recovery. Amorim will continue to ponder things, but this is far from a headache, because the rule seems to be well established: if Cisse plays, he tends to score.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Aston Villa's NSWE ownership deserve significant praise for helping to ease the pressure on the club's Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) standing in recent years.
  • That is according to former Villa chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the owners have tackled the matter by working hard to increase the club's revenue streams.
  • This comes after a recent reports from The Orange Ledger indicated that the Villans have used just 73.8 per cent of their allowed 85 per cent of revenue on their first-team squad.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa's NSWE ownership deserve significant praise for helping to ease the pressure on the club's Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) standing in recent years.

That is according to former Villa chief executive Keith Wyness, speaking exclusively to Football Insider, who believes that the owners have tackled the matter by working hard to increase the club's revenue streams.

This comes after a recent reports from The Orange Ledger indicated that the Villans have used just 73.8 per cent of their allowed 85 per cent of revenue on their first-team squad.

Wyness believes that is a result of several "innovative" money-making schemes from the club, which have stretched their revenue further, rather than tackling the glitch by cutting costs.

The Orange Ledger's report ranked Unai Emery's side ninth in the Premier League in terms of available SCR headroom, and outlined that they have around £62million of free space available.

This is a far cry from Villa's standing in previous years, when they have consistently had to make player decisions based around their financial standing.

Villa's former chief Wyness - who served as CEO at Villa Park between 2016 and 2018 and now runs a consultancy business advising elite clubs - believes that Villa have made an "incredible" turnaround with their SCR standing.

They have even been able to turn their fortunes around without overhauling their squad with cheap additions, and are still competing in the Champions League as a result.

Speaking on the latest edition of Football Insider's Inside Track podcast, Wyness explained how it is Wes Edens and Nassef Sawiris who deserve all the credit.

Sources indicate that "Look, it's a great story and they deserve full credit for what they've done. Rather than attack it at the cost cutting situation, they've gone at the top level and tried to increase revenues and that's the right way to approach it," he said.

"It's a really good story. It's one of innovative and visionary support from the owners and good execution from the executive team as well. So I think Villa deserves a lot of credit for what they've done.

In a recent development, "Certainly to be ninth right now is incredible compared to where they were and we've been keeping an eye on and they've been in and out of barriers with PSR and SCR et cetera. So good luck to them, they're still competing on the pitch, they're in Europe and they deserve it.".

Former Villa scout Bryan King told Football Insider earlier this week that his former club would now have to pay "£60m" if they wanted to re-sign former striker Donyell Malen.

Roma triggered their option to buy the Dutchman for £21.5m at the start of the summer, and he has since excelled and is sitting at the top of the Serie A scoring charts.

King believes that Villa made a mistake by letting Malen go, and feels that it would now be beyond their reach to be able to buy him back.

The 27-year-old has notched 12 goals and two assists from just 11 league games so far this term, and has quickly established himself as Roma's star man.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was the afternoon when Xabi Alonso’s Chelsea went from swashbuckling to stoic, thrilling to tenacious.

For all Alonso’s attacking vigour at the start of his reign, there can have been no more symbolically satisfying victory under the new coach than this resolute win at Everton – the most vivid example of an increasingly impressive transformation.

Industry observers note that this was what Alonso described as “winning in a different way”. A triumph amid the adversity of losing goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez to what appears to be a serious injury after a head collision with Jarrad Branthwaite is just one facet of why the joyous visiting supporters might consider this an early turning point.

Where recently they wilted, on Saturday they thrived in securing a first Premier League clean sheet for nine months.

Much more of this and the adjectives which were splattered across Chelsea during the golden years of José Mourinho – solid, robust and dogged – will be part of the Stamford Bridge lexicon once more.

“Just one day,” Alonso warned, both acclaiming the importance of the win while wisely preaching caution. “It will be key when we manage 10 clean sheets, even though this one feels good. We need to repeat it again and again, but the mentality was very good. Sometimes it is not to play nice, it is to play good – to win second balls, and to be efficient. We needed one of these: a clean sheet and a win.”.

Sources indicate that asked about Martinez’s condition, Alonso noted: “It was a concussion, but beyond that I do not know. I have only seen one clip of the incident, so we need to wait.

“What we know is that he left the stadium conscious and is now in hospital undergoing precautionary tests.

“We need to wait. Hopefully it will not be too serious, but at the moment we just have to wait.”.

Alonso is speedily shifting perceptions of this previously underperforming bunch, the Stamford Bridge culture on and off the pitch already unrecognisable from a few months ago.

It was Chelsea’s trip to Everton last season which facilitated the endgame of Liam Rosenior’s short, but generally hideous reign.

For those who tried to banish memories, it was a darkly comical period when Chelsea’s players were paying their respect to stationary footballs, seemingly finding upcoming ways to stand in front of travelling fans to apologise for meek and rancid performances.

Recent findings suggest that how different the scenes after Pedro Neto’s double on Merseyside – a success built on those old-fashioned and too often underestimated qualities of character and application before the artists had the final say. These are the wins that build connections and trust between players and supporters, especially during the getting-to-know-you period of a managerial tenure. While neutrals mutter about a generally disappointing spectacle, the players and supporters return home clutching three points believing they have fought together in the trenches.

It cannot be overlooked how this win owed a debt to the erratic refereeing of Paul Tierney, especially the amnesty he offered to Morgan Rogers on the stroke of half-time.

Industry observers note that already booked, Rogers was fortunate not to receive a second caution for a lunge on James Garner which took the man after the ball. A replica challenge by Everton’s Harrison Armstrong had warranted a yellow card in Tierney’s world just 21 minutes earlier.

The home team’s argument that this was a potential game changer was supported when the England midfielder was inevitably involved in the move which led to Neto breaking through 44 seconds into the second half – a lead Chelsea never looked like surrendering as Everton’s attacking limitations were exposed.

Mike Penders deputised for the stricken Martínez – conscious but taken to hospital as a precaution – and was well-protected.

As much as Alonso’s artistry as a midfield maestro is presumed to define him as a coach, one cannot help but believe there are many who underestimate him as a football student. He was never going to return to England clinging to one idea given his previous Premier League experience, and he intuitively knew an away game at Everton was one for foot soldiers.

Alonso’s name has not echoed so loudly across the Mersey since he played a few miles down the road from Everton’s upcoming home. After several calamitous appointments, those fans can believe their team are in safe hands again.

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Everton vs Chelsea.

Chelsea return to Premier League action this weekend looking to harness the momentum of their emphatic 5-1 victory over Bournemouth before the international break. That Stamford Bridge masterclass ended a frustrating three-match winless streak and was built upon braces from Joao Pedro and Jordan Henderson, alongside another strike from summer signing Morgan Rogers.

Yet the true catalyst for the resurgence was the return of Moises Caicedo. Having shaken off the calf problem that hindered his early-season involvement, the midfielder anchored the side’s win. While defensive vulnerabilities persist - extending an unwanted run of league matches without a clean sheet back to January - the victory offered clear signs of progress under their head coach, Xabi Alonso.

In a recent development, next up is a notoriously difficult trip to Merseyside to face Everton in Saturday’s lunchtime fixture. Historically, Everton have proven to be a formidable stumbling block for the capital club, particularly on home turf. Everton enter the weekend unbeaten in eight of their last nine home encounters against Chelsea, a stretch that has seen the Londoners fail to score on seven visits and suffer six defeats, including a chastening 3-0 reverse last term that spelt the end for Liam Rosenior.

David Moyes will demand a sharper defensive showing from his side this time around, following a frustrating 2-2 draw with Hull City where a 2-1 lead slipped away. Even so, Everton’s broader defensive record at home offers encouragement, having kept clean sheets in two of their opening three league fixtures at their base.

With both teams eager to build consistency, Saturday’s clash pits Chelsea’s newly found attacking spark against an opponent that traditionally relishes this fixture.

How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match.
  • That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.

The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match.

That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February.

Now that we’re past the halfway mark of the league phase, the 36 Champions League clubs have a strong indication as to where they’re likely to finish, and what more needs to be done to achieve their targets.

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

At present, Manchester City occupy the final position for automatic passage to the round of 16, with Enzo Maresca’s side on 10 points, averaging two per game.

That means the projected points tally required for a top-eight placing is 16, so Liverpool would need to aim for at least four points from their remaining three matches against Porto (home), Inter Milan (away) and Lens (home).

The two Anfield fixtures are against teams placed 22nd and 34th respectively, so the Reds would be fully expected to win both of those.

(Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images).

The visit to the San Siro is likely to be much tougher, but LFC beat Inter at the famous venue last season, and a repeat result would probably be enough to guarantee a top-eight finish with one game to spare.

That’d give Iraola the luxury of being able to rest key players for the concluding fixture against Lens, which falls between Premier League matches against Manchester United and Everton.

With Liverpool also still going strong in the Carabao Cup and plausibly making it to a two-legged semi-final in the opening weeks of 2027, any opportunity to rotate the squad in January must be embraced.

The picture can obviously change over the final three matchdays, but right now it seems probable that if the Reds beat Porto and get a result away to Inter, they could be effectively or even mathematically assured of a top-eight finish by the time they host Lens.

That objective is well within reach for Iraola’s side, and avoiding the play-off round in February is a must.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Firm, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

According to recent reports, in Los Angeles, California, far away from the small English village of Mirfield where he was born, Stewart achieved world fame. He was 47 years old when he landed the role of a lifetime in the legendary science fiction series Star Trek: Playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," he stepped into the shoes of the legendary Captain James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner.

According to recent reports, stewart brought a calm, measured and distinctly British presence that swiftly made Picard a fan favorite and a cult figure in the Star Trek universe. He returned to the role decades later in the spin-off series "Star Trek: Picard," which ended in 2023, proving the character's enduring appeal.

According to recent reports, as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, he led the crew of the starship Enterprise, a spaceship with the sizeable mission: "To explore strange new worlds. To seek out new life and new civilizations" — and most importantly, "to boldly go where no man has gone before!".

Stewart's interest in acting was sparked in the early 1950s when a teacher asked him to recite a work by Shakespeare. His passion for Shakespeare stayed with him until the end.

Industry observers note that his parents were far removed from the glamor of the theatrical world. His father was a highly respected officer in the British Army during World War II, but at home, he was an abusive husband, and young Patrick had to helplessly witness repeated violence against his mother. Stewart wrote about his experiences with domestic violence in The Guardian in 2009. The stage, he confessed there, seemed to him "a far safer place" than reality; he saw acting as a way to escape his home life.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Patrick began acting at the age of 12. At 16, he left school early and, thanks to a scholarship, studied acting in Bristol, England. Along the way, he worked as a journalist. In 1965, he became an official member of the Royal Shakespeare Manufacturer, and remained with the theather company from 1966 to 1982. Such was his passion for the great English playwright and lyricist that he even shared his sonnets on his Twitter account during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic.

It has been revealed that stewart dazzled the theater world with his own stage adaptation of Charles Dickens' 1843 tale "A Christmas Carol." He played more than 30 roles himself. After its 1987 premiere in Stewart's hometown of Mirfield, the one-man show became a critics' favorite and a long-running hit on Broadway in New York.

According to recent reports, in the same year,  Stewart went from being a stage actor to an international TV star. Star Trek producer Robert Justman offered him the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, one of the main characters in a fresh edition of the popular TV series "Star Trek: The Next Generation.".

The successful Shakespearean hesitated. Until then, he had never worked in Hollywood. But his agent encouraged him to accept the role, Stewart recalled in a 2020 interview with the German newspaper Die Welt. "You can accept the offer as a start for now. It won't be a significant deal, you can't revive a series as iconic as Star Trek anyway.".

But his agent was to be proven wrong: Stewart led the Starship Enterprise through its galactic adventures for seven seasons and four full-length feature films. The TV series had astronomical success on Earth in a very short time. At first, the producers were at odds as to whether Stewart's British accent could really fit the role of commander of a US starship in the 24th century, but it soon became impossible to imagine the series without the subtly diplomatic Captain Picard, who often quoted Shakespeare while at the helm. It seemed as if all the time he had spent as a Shakespearean actor had prepared him to command the Enterprise, Stewart once remarked with a wink. When the cult series ended in 1994, he had ruled out ever returning to the Enterprise's command center.

According to recent reports, in 2010, the actor was knighted by the Queen of England. Stewart considered it the greatest honor of his career to stand alongside acting greats such as Sir Laurence Olivier and Sir Alec Guinness.

Beyond the screen, Stewart has long used his voice for social and human rights causes. In recent years, he has drawn attention to issues such as violence against women, age discrimination and the protection of children.

In a June 2020 interview, "Playboy" asked the New York resident whether he was considering retiring from acting. "Never! That would mean giving up my life," replied Stewart, who was approaching his 80th birthday at the time. He was filming the second of three seasons of "Star Trek: Picard." The series ends with a final episode in which the retired Starfleet admiral makes his last appearance. In the series, Picard retires to his family vineyard in France but is drawn back into space to confront new threats to the Federation.

It has been revealed that this series also showcases Stewart's affection for his pit bull, Ginger. In "Star Trek: Picard," Picard also has a pit bull, a loyal four-legged companion named Number One — a deliberate reference to Stewart's real-life love of the breed. For his efforts to combat prejudice against pit bulls and to support their adoption, Stewart was honored by the US animal welfare organization ASPCA, among others.

In 2024, he published his memoir "Making it So." In it, he recounts his passion for theater and his love of Shakespeare.

Industry observers note that now, at the age of 86, the British actor has finally departed for another galaxy. Farewell, Patrick Stewart!

Rodrigo Muniz can help Fulham navigate their issues in front of goal.

The Cottagers are one of the worst in the Premier League when it comes to scoring, with only Sunderland (eight) and Nottingham Forest (nine) scoring fewer than Fulham's 11 goals.

Brazilian striker Muniz has not been favoured by Alvaro Arbeloa this season at all, with the 25-year-old managing just one start from nine appearances in the league.

However, his lack of opportunities is becoming increasingly difficult to justify given Fulham's struggles in the final third.

And his recent performances have only further added to the debate over Fulham's striker position.

With data showing he is the better option going forward for the London side.

Even in his limited minutes, Muniz has already proven to be better in front of goal compared to Gonzalo Garcia.

In 179 minutes, Muniz has racked up 0.99 xG, with an xGOT of 1.61 as per FotMob, showing that with his shot placement, he improves the quality of his chances.

From those chances, he has netted two goals in the Premier League, which is more than his Spanish counterpart has scored this campaign.

Garcia has been frustrating in front of goal, with his shooting erratic. In direct contrast to Muniz, he has drastically made his own chances worse.

From 4.07 xG, he has managed just 0.95 xGOT, suggesting his shot placement has significantly reduced the quality of the chances he has been given.

If Fulham are to get wins over the line, they cannot afford to continue trusting Garcia, who has started 10 of the 11 games so far.

It is time for Muniz to get a long run of games leading the line, and the London side may finally begin climbing the table.

Anytime a player's data is analysed despite limited minutes, there will be concerns over the sample size.

However, throughout his time in the Premier League, he has proven his clinical ability.

In 2023-24, he had an xG and xGOT difference of +1.01, while in 2024-25 that total stood at +2.41.

Last season was not quite there, as he had a negative total of -2.48.

But nonetheless, the trend is that he is often able to make more out of his chances than the original value suggests.

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 18:45 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 03:20 EST, 25 November 2026.

Jude Bellingham underlined his class once more with a stunning goal as Real Madrid came from behind to thump PSV Eindhoven 5-1.

With Real trailing 1-0 at half-time, the England superstar - who started as a substitute to rest - was one of three changes made by Jose Mourinho and his impact was felt 15 minutes later in an emphatic style.

Recent findings suggest that collecting a loose ball from around 25 yards outside the box, Bellingham controlled it with his left foot, before flicking it up with his right foot and volleying it with the outside of that boot into the far corner of the PSV goal. The pace and precision of the strike was breathtaking as it flew past Matej Kovar and hit the inside of the post before going in.

It was a strike that was befitting of any match, and it proved to be the decisive one as that made it 2-1 to the hosts before they later ran riot.

Speaking post-match, Bellingham was clear where he ranked that finish, declaring: 'I think this was the best goal of my life.'.

He later elaborated to TNT Sports about his goal: 'They're [his goals] normally a lot closer, aren't they,' he joked.

SENSATIONAL JUDE BELLINGHAM 🤯Bellingham gives the hosts the lead with a magnificent volley 🔥 📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/WdP6ULx8wE.

Jude Bellingham (right) scored a stunning volley to inspire Real Madrid to beat PSV Eindhoven.

Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead with this beautiful right-footed volley.

PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovar could only watch on as the ball flew past him and go into the net.

'That one was a nice one, it popped up for me nicely and I just thought I'd hit it with the outside of my boot.

'I'm not one for smashing the ball too hard and it was a nice moment and notable for the win as well.'.

Bellingham's performance, he also set up Vinicius Jr for the fifth goal, was acknowledged by Mourinho and Real captain Fede Valverde, who scored their equaliser, post-match too.

'Obviously Jude is a different type of player and he gave us what we didn't have in the first half,' Mourinho stated. 'He changed the game, scored an incredible goal.'.

Industry observers note that valverde concurred declaring: 'He did well. We were struggling to keep the ball behind their midfielders and when Jude came in he gave us that tranquillity to control possession.'.

The strike comes a day after Daily Mail Sport reported that the 23-year-old is in advance talks over a upcoming Real Madrid contract that will make him one of the best-paid players in Europe.

Madrid have been eager to tie down the in-form England midfielder beyond his current contract, understood to be worth around £12.5million a year after tax, which runs until 2029, in recognition of his performances.

Talks were initiated in September over an extension until 2031 and have been progressing well since with sources at Madrid confident they are close to reaching a conclusion.

Bellingham is in advance contract talks with Real Madrid over signing an extension until 2031.

Bellingham is expected to be handed improved terms to put him on par with team-mate Vinicius Jr, who agreed a new deal last summer reputedly on around £500,000 a week after tax.

As for Tuesday's win over PSV, Real are now top of the Champions League league phase standings after maintaining their 100 per cent record in the competition this season with a fifth-straight win.

1. Erling Haaland, Manchester City: £510,000 per week.

2. Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid: £503,000 per week.

3. Vinicius Jr, Real Madrid: £500,000 per week.

4. Harry Kane, Bayern Munich: £402,000 per week.

5. Virgil van Dijk, Liverpool: £350,000 per week.

However, they didn't have it all their own way as PSV took a deserved lead in the 32nd minute from the penalty spot, with 37-year-old captain Ivan Perisic showing all his experience, ignoring the whistles ringing out around the Bernabeu before sending Thibaut Courtois the wrong way.

They almost doubled their lead before the break as the unmarked Kodai Sano glanced a header off target as the visitors continued to cause Real serious problems.

Real equalised five minutes after the break, thanks to Arda Guler's quick-thinking, with the Turkish midfielder flicking a backheeled pass to Valverde in the area, who steered his first-time shot into the bottom corner.

Real's fans were on their feet 10 minutes later, scarcely believing what they had seen, while Bellingham's team-mates looked similarly shell-shocked.

Marc Cucurella walked away with his head in his hands in wonder while the other Real players rushed to congratulate the scorer.

Real took command after Bellingham's goal and punished a loose pass in the PSV defence, Guler finding the unmarked Mbappe to extend the France forward's scoring run to seven successive Champions League appearances.

Mbappe added his second before Vinicius rounded off a resounding victory from Bellingham's pass, underlining the Spanish side's credentials as serious contenders to take Paris Saint-Germain's crown.

Tom Brady is unlikely to invest "meaningful money" when coming aboard as a minority shareholder at Chelsea.

That is according to former Manchester City financial adviser Stefan Borson, who exclusively told Football Insider that Chelsea fans should not be getting too excited over the newly introduced developments.

After cutting ties with Birmingham City, the seven-time Super Bowl winner has now opened talks with those behind the scenes at Stamford Bridge.

It is understood that Clearlake Capital would remain in full control, still owning 86.5 per cent of the Blues, with Brady given no voting rights.

This deal appears to have been in the works for quite some time. Brady was spotted celebrating with the Chelsea players after winning the Club World Cup in the summer of 2025.

There is excitement building amongst the fans about what his introduction could mean for the club, but it may not be as thrilling as many think.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Borson expects Brady to make very little impact when coming aboard as a minority owner at Chelsea.

Sources indicate that "The way these deals work, I think Tom Brady was given the shares in Birmingham previously. They were non-voting shares," he mentioned.

"So I think it might be slightly different at Chelsea, but Chelsea is a much bigger organisation. He's not going to put in meaningful money.

"It's much more about being a figurehead and about seeing the upside of that. As far as I understand it, Tom Brady is not somebody who effectively fronts a fund.

"If you look at someone like Ashton Kutcher, he's effectively a major technology investor through his personality, but also he's built a fund.

"I don't think Tom Brady is a supporting equivalent of that. So if he would just be a figurehead associated with Chelsea, I think it would have very little impact to be honest, either way.".

That would likely see the iconic NFL figure own a tiny share at Stamford Bridge, possibly as small as one per cent to come aboard.

This kind of money is simply a drop in the ocean for the Blues' current owners, but they would never say no to further investment.

Changes are still taking shape after Todd Boehly's exit, and it has been reiterated that the two stories have no correlation in West London.

Oliver Glasner will have the ability to add signings to the Nottingham Forest squad during the January transfer window.

That is according to former Manchester City financial adviser Stefan Borson, who exclusively told Football Insider that Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) shouldn't be a concern, but Forest will need to be sensible with additions.

It is understood that Glasner is targeting as many as five new additions in the January window, having recently met with Evangelos Marinakis.

The manager travelled to London for a three-hour meeting on the squad's day off on Monday, 23 November, to discuss potential signings.

With the Reds sitting 17th in the Premier League table, it is clear that the boss needs reinforcements for a successful second-half of the campaign.

Most recently, Glasner criticised the players in the squad who are unable to speak English fluently after years in the country, so he won't want more of the same.

Speaking exclusively to Football Insider, Borson has poured cold water on the idea of five signings, but alleviated any fears of SCR breaches.

Industry observers note that "I doubt there's space for five. It's not just transfer fees, it's wages as well. I've not looked at what their SCR position is," he said.

"But it's very hard for any team to fail SCR just because you've got an 85 per cent cap under the Premier League rules, and you can always deal with a breach under the UEFA rules if you are in UEFA competition.

"At the moment, the sad reality for Forest is it doesn't look like they're going to be in UEFA competition next season.

"So I suspect they're pretty close to the 85 per cent, but it's probably not that big a deal. But five players is a lot.

"Maybe there is a proposal to make a sale in the summer. So these sorts of things change the equation. But it doesn't look to me as if they'll buy five players.

"The squad's already quite substantial anyway. The wage bill's quite high relative to revenue. So I doubt there'll be five players coming.".

With his outburst at those who are unable to speak fluent English, fans have narrowed it down to Ibrahim Sangare and Nicolas Dominguez.

So both players could be on the chopping block in the next couple of transfer windows.

In January, a new goalkeeper is understood to be at the top of the list, as well as a left-wing-back, central midfielder and an attacker.

The latter would be imperative to helping Morgan Gibbs-White and Liam Delap shine at the City Ground, and that will be important for Forest's success.
